html:
SMTO-SCH-0018 — A repeating schedule can't also have a fixed next time

GUID: 3c6cde20-370b-4af0-ad15-e8d55e58eb62
Slug: schedule-calendar-fields-conflict
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • This schedule repeats on a pattern, like every weekday at 9:00, so SMTO works out each run time itself. The change also tried to set a separate next time or gap between runs, so it was not saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Schedules, select Edit on this schedule, and set the timing with Repeat, Starts, the time and the days you want. Then save. The editor sends only the repeat pattern, which is the one way a repeating schedule can be changed.
  2. If you asked the Agent to change it, describe the pattern only, for example "every Monday at 8:00 AM", without also giving a separate next run time. Giving both a pattern and a one-off next time is what caused this conflict.
  3. If you need a one-time run instead, set Repeat to Does not repeat and choose the date and time. A schedule that does not repeat is the kind that takes a single fixed time.

What success looks like

  • The schedule saves and its Next run shows the first time that matches your pattern.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, along with the timing you wanted.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A calendar schedule update was rejected because it also supplied next_run_at or interval_seconds, which calendar recurrence computes itself.

What this means

  • An effective calendar schedule update supplies a direct next_run_at or interval_seconds override. Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.

Why this can happen

  • An effective calendar schedule update supplies a direct next_run_at or interval_seconds override.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect schedule_type and remove competing direct timing values.

How to fix it

  • normalized_event_update rejects next_run_at and interval_seconds when the effective schedule_type is calendar. Drop both fields from the update and express the timing through recurrence (start_date, time, pattern, end) and timezone; next_run_at is then derived by next_calendar().
  • Remove direct next_run_at and interval overrides; the calendar recurrence computes these fields.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The recurrence alone computes the intended next occurrence and interval behavior.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
